messages:
maya: quick poll — we need a recommendation for the internal API shape for next quarter: push gRPC+proto everywhere, or keep JSON/REST at the edge and do proto conversion at the gateway? pros/cons? 
ben: +1 to keeping JSON at the edge. most clients are web/mobile, and hell to debug if every team has to handle proto. 
linh: counterpoint: gRPC gives typed contracts, smaller payloads, and better streaming support for some long-lived connections. saves CPU for some heavy services.
sam: can we compromise: gRPC for service-to-service + internal-platform deps, JSON for public/SDK edges and let gateway transcode? that's what I'm leaning toward.maya: what about operational stuff — quotas, routing, and console signals? if gateway transcodes, we lose some typed telemetry unless we surface proto fields in headers.yan: that's the tricky bit. if gateway does headless conversion, console loses per-field metrics unless we add explicit mapping rules. it becomes brittle as proto evolves.
ben: true, but mapping everything to headers is noisy. we should instead define a small set of routing keys (tenant, intent, priority) that the gateway extracts and emits to tracing/metrics, regardless of wire format.
linh: agreed on routing keys. but for quota accounting we also need stable IDs in the payload. proto makes that explicit. with JSON we need validation layers to ensure fields exist.
sam: operationally, can we have a lightweight schema registry for JSON endpoints that mirrors proto fields? gateway can validate against it. that avoids forcing teams to use proto libs.maya: UX for rollouts — if we switch a service from JSON to proto, how do we canary without breaking consumers? gateway-transcode can help by routing a percentage to proto-only backend and translating responses for JSON clients.ben: yeah but that adds latency and more edge complexity. every request might hit transcoding costs. we could do canary behind the service mesh (internal traffic) first.
linh: latency numbers matter. I ran a quick bench — Envoy transcoding adds ~6–9ms p50 for small payloads on our test infra. for high QPS routes that accumulates.ma: can we rely on batching or streaming to amortize cost? not for normal request/response flows.
ryan: telemetry: console wants token-level cost breakdown + per-route latencies. if transcoding hides model-routing keys, we need the gateway to emit enriched spans with proto metadata. doable but requires a mapping config and per-route tests.
ben: mapping config = another source of drift. who owns it? infra team or product teams? we need ownership model.
sam: infra should provide defaults and a status table; owning teams opt in for custom mappings. similar to how we do quotas now.
linh: also consider developer ergonomics — codegen story for proto is great for backend teams (typed stubs). forcing that on frontend teams is a blocker. we should avoid making frontend compile proto unless necessary.maya: proposed recommendation draft: 1) default: JSON/REST at the edge + typed gRPC internally for new services; 2) gateway does optional transpile/transcode with explicit mapping configs for routing/quota keys; 3) define 3 standard routing keys (tenant, feature_flag, priority) that are mandated across proto/json; 4) infra owns default mapping and exposes console UI to inspect/override; 5) canary flows happen within service mesh first, then gateway canary with translation off for traffic that supports proto.
ben: looks reasonable. minor tweak: make mapping configs Git-backed and validated by CI.
sam: +1 for git-backed mappings. also add a small shim library for frontends that gives typed access to routing keys without full proto deps.
ryan: I'll sketch the console changes: add a mapping inspector panel and a transcoding latency column per-route. also show quota attribution source (gateway vs service).
deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/mapping-service v0.3 -> staging at 1702501200 by @ryan :rocket:
linh: will prepare the bench and a short doc showing latency/CPU tradeoffs for the RFC.maya: great — I'll turn this into a short RFC and post in #eng-platform tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
